finding: Count-weighted covariate-pattern compression for adjacent-category and continuation-ratio fits

finding: Make damped Newton-Raphson the default for adjacent-category and continuation-ratio fits
reason: Bench, Phase 0 (run 44048167550, same EDI build, 20 ABBA blocks): not faster, ratio 1.56 (damped Newton 56% slower than the L-BFGS default; 95% interval -56.7% to -54.5%). Automatic reject (owner 2026-11-19). The Newton-default question itself stays with algorithm_choice_audit.md TODO-12 in v1.2.0-TODO-23, which is not closed by this.

finding: BLDM + complete Karmarkar-Karp for p = 1 optimal allocation
reason: Plausible but narrow: only p = 1 and the |sum difference| kinds, with an exponential certification tail near n = 50-60. The exact enumeration solver for n <= ~30 (algorithm_choice_audit.md TODO-20, in v1.2.0-TODO-23) covers the MILP range first; revisit for n > 30, p = 1 after it lands. (Was cited under v1.2.0-TODO-23.)

finding: Low-rank convex MIQCP via the CRAN scip package for DesignFixedOptimal
reason: New optional dependency, no benchmark, applies_at_edi_sizes unknown. The MILP is used only up to n = 20 (EDI_OPTIMAL_DEFAULT_LINEARIZATION_MAX_N, helper_optimal_milp_solvers.R:25), which the planned exact enumerator (audit TODO-20, v1.2.0-TODO-23) supersedes up to ~30; the MIQP formulation is already noted in catalog §12 TODO-2. (Was cited under v1.2.0-TODO-23.)

finding: HiGHS instead of GLPK as the MILP backend for optimal designs
reason: Unquantified, new dependency, and the source itself says results depend on the formulation; GLPK runs only at n <= 20 (helper_optimal_milp_solvers.R:25), where audit TODO-20's enumerator (v1.2.0-TODO-23) is the planned replacement. Revisit as one arm of that benchmark if MILPs are still used beyond the enumeration cap. (Was cited under v1.2.0-TODO-23.)

finding: Bayesian-bootstrap ZOIB replicate: C++ weighted beta MLE instead of betareg
reason: compute_estimate_with_bootstrap_weights fits the interior block with the formula betareg::betareg per replicate (inference_proportion_zero_one_inflated_beta.R:286-296) although fast_beta_regression_weighted_cpp exists and is used by the beta class (inference_proportion_beta.R:278). The ZOIB likelihood is separable, so the beta block MLE is the same; the two weighted logits (:260-275) only feed cached zero/one coefficients (:330-331). Skipping them is audit TODO-13 (v1.2.0-TODO-23); the betareg swap has no TODO.

finding: Vectorize the per-row rbeta loop in the ZOIB parametric-bootstrap simulator
reason: Real but small: the loop at inference_proportion_zero_one_inflated_beta.R:791-801 draws u as a vector first and interleaves no other RNG, so a vectorized rbeta should be identical(); but it saves only O(n) interpreted iterations next to a C++ ZOIB refit per replicate. Fold into the ZOIB BB TODO (finding beta-regression-mle#43925959437.1) if that is approved, gated on identical() under a fixed seed.

finding: Make IRLS the default of the fast_logistic_regression R wrappers
reason: The exported wrappers default optimization_alg = "lbfgs" (helper_glm_fit.R:852, :923) while the C++ kernels default to "irls" (RcppExports.R:1854/1862); KK21 calls the with_var wrapper per covariate (design_seq_one_by_one_KK21.R:431, design_seq_one_by_one_KK21_stepwise.R:345). Not covered by audit TODO-12, whose list omits logistic. Changing an exported default and possibly KK21 separation handling needs an A/B.

finding: Route fractional-logit estimate_only glm.fit branch to C++ IRLS
reason: The glm.fit(quasibinomial) branch (inference_proportion_fractional_logit.R:165) runs only when harden = FALSE, and harden defaults to TRUE (:140) with no internal caller setting it FALSE, so this is a cold opt-in path; the default path already uses fast_logistic_regression_cpp (:257).

finding: Exact subset dynamic program for small-n optimal blocking
reason: The optimal-blocks MILP is documented at ~79 s per solve at n = 16, B = 4 (design_fixed_optimal_blocks.R:138-140) and is re-solved per replay draw. Speeding this solve is already scheduled as the optimal-blocks reformulation benchmark (catalog §12 TODO-5 via algorithm_choice_audit.md TODO-20, v1.2.0-TODO-23); the DP should be added as an arm there. Owner may want to pull it forward since it is exact and needs no A/B.

finding: Exact blossom matching fast path when every block has size 2
reason: When n = 2B the objective is minimum-weight perfect matching, and nbpMatching is already an import (DESCRIPTION:78) used via nonbimatch in helper_matching.R:44; solve_optimal_blocks still uses the MILP. Exact, polynomial and small, but only for user-chosen B = n/2. No existing TODO.

finding: HiGHS as an open-source MILP backend for optimal blocks
reason: Unquantified for this model; ROI.plugin.highs MILP support is unconfirmed by the finding itself, and it adds a dependency. roi_solver is a closed set (helper_optimal_milp_solvers.R:30). Relevant only beyond the small-n range that the reformulation/DP work in v1.2.0-TODO-23 targets. (Was cited under v1.2.0-TODO-23.)

finding: Exact cardinality-constrained MSSC (SDP branch-and-cut) for blocking
reason: Needs MATLAB/Gurobi-class tooling with no linked code, and only helps at n much larger than 20, which EDI's exact blocking does not target; the finding itself recommends not pursuing it.

finding: fastcluster::hclust drop-in for the K-way hold-out step
reason: The step costs ~6-21 ms per replay draw (finding's own numbers), and fastcluster may resolve ward.D2 ties differently, which can change the held-out subjects and so the blocks (design_fixed_optimal_blocks.R:468); a new dependency for no measured win.

finding: Draw the double-bootstrap outer x inner set once for all grid alphas
reason: Confirmed: ci_calibrated_bootstrap redraws n_outer outer resamples with inner bootstraps inside the alpha-grid loop (inference_all_abstract_non_param_boot.R:2001-2016), ~5x the needed refits. Covered by algorithm_choice_audit.md TODO-26 (double-bootstrap, §9 TODO-2) in v1.2.0-TODO-23; the grid-hoist half keeps the procedure, so the owner could split it out ahead of the harness.

finding: Dense bitset instead of unordered_set in sample_group_units
reason: Bit-identical but negligible end to end (the finding says so); rejection + unordered_set is at exchangeable_resampling_draws.cpp:81. The partial Fisher-Yates half (catalog §7 TODO-2) is unscheduled and changes the stream. Revisit only if profiling shows subsampling draws matter.

finding: Batched bounded random integers (Brackett-Rozinsky & Lemire) for bootstrap indices
reason: Unquantified at EDI sizes, needs 64-bit words while RRng is 32-bit MT19937, changes seed-pinned streams, and index generation is small next to per-replicate refits. Belongs with the RNG-throughput measurement (performance_profiling_and_upgrades.md TODO-149, in v1.2.0-TODO-11). (Was cited under v1.2.0-TODO-11.)

finding: Anytime-valid Monte Carlo testing by betting for the BRT sequential p-value
reason: Changes the reported p-value (keeps_estimator: no), so it is a policy change that needs the owner's decision. The current per-look Clopper-Pearson stop is compute_two_sided_brt_pval_with_sequential_mc (inference_all_abstract_rand_bootstrap.R:930). Covered by the anytime-results item v1.2.0-TODO-34 (with performance_profiling_and_upgrades.md TODO-156 Besag-Clifford); add the BRT p-value path to its scope.

finding: KK CLMM Bayesian bootstrap: cluster-weighted native GH objective; clmm weight semantics
reason: Possible wrong output, not just speed: weighted_ordinal_random_intercept_fit passes row weights to ordinal::clmm (helper_ordinal_mixed_fit.R:127-134), which per the cited clmm source weights each observation inside the group integral, not each group's log-integral as the cluster Bayesian bootstrap implies. No existing TODO. Placed in v1.0.6 as a bounded check; the native-kernel fix changes replicate results, so the owner must decide whether that weighting is a bug.

finding: Adaptive GH with exact AQ gradient (Stringer 2024) for ordinal GLMM/CLMM
reason: Adaptive GH is already the tracked item performance_profiling_and_upgrades.md TODO-153 (with audit TODO-40's quadrature dial), scheduled in v1.2.0-TODO-11; Stringer's implicit-gradient method answers that item's gradient objection and should be cited there. The aghqmm code has no license, so derive from the paper.

finding: C++ partial Fisher-Yates kernel for block_ra_batch
reason: block_ra_batch is already vectorized R (design_fixed_blocking.R:16, used by blocking/cluster/optimal-blocks designs), so the old replicate(randomizr) cost that audit TODO-21 (v1.2.0-TODO-22) targeted is mostly gone; the remaining constant-factor gain is unmeasured and changes seed-pinned draws. Profile first under that item. (Was cited under v1.2.0-TODO-22.)

finding: Batched bounded random integers for Fisher-Yates shuffles
reason: Same as the bootstrap-index finding: measured only with 64-bit generators, changes the seed-pinned R/Python stream, and the shuffle is rarely dominant (rerandomization spends O(np) per draw on balance). Revisit with the RNG-throughput item (performance TODO-149 in v1.2.0-TODO-11). (Was cited under v1.2.0-TODO-11.)

finding: Clogit reservoir logistic: C++ weighted IRLS instead of R glm.fit
reason: fit_clogit_reservoir_logit calls stats::glm.fit with weights and an offset (inference_incidence_KK_cond_logit_glmm_abstract.R:604-612) in every bootstrap replicate and null refit. The weights argument the finding wants already exists: fast_logistic_regression_weighted_cpp(X, y, weights, fixed_idx, fixed_values, ...) (RcppExports.R:1858), and the offset is the fixed coordinate. Not in audit TODO-19 (which has cpoisson, not clogit).

finding: Weighted C++ cpoisson-combined Newton instead of R optim BFGS
reason: Confirmed at inference_count_KK_cond_poisson.R:2139 (optim BFGS on R-coded NLL/score per replicate). Already scheduled: algorithm_choice_audit.md TODO-19 (weighted C++ cpoisson-combined, catalog §10 TODO-2) in v1.2.0-TODO-22, with the step-halving half in audit TODO-24 (v1.1.0-TODO-50).

finding: Exponential-cone interior-point (ECOS/Clarabel) solver for log/identity-binomial MLE
reason: A robustness idea with a new solver dependency and no measured gain over EDI's own active-set projection and KKT gate; probably slower per fit than IRLS. It is a candidate arm for the log-binomial constrained solver in algorithm_choice_audit.md TODO-32 (v1.2.0-TODO-23), not its own item. (Was cited under v1.2.0-TODO-23.)

finding: Analytic score and Hessian for log/identity-binomial instead of finite differences
reason: Still FD: score h = 1e-6 and Hessian h = 1e-4 stencils at fast_log_binomial_regression.cpp:840-920. Already scheduled as algorithm_choice_audit.md TODO-14 (catalog §1 TODO-1) in v1.1.0-TODO-50; closed forms exist in R (edi_log_binomial_kkt_terms) to cross-check against.

finding: Factor the information matrix once (reuse FullPivLU or LDLT) for vcov
reason: Microseconds per fit at p <= 20, and the FullPivLU check plus inverse() pair is deliberate for bit-compatibility (comment at _helper_functions_core.h:724-748). Tracked under performance_profiling_and_upgrades.md TODO-155 (v1.2.0-TODO-11); try lu.inverse() there with a vcov-fixture A/B. (Was cited under v1.2.0-TODO-11.)

finding: Breslow hazard and R Cox NLL via one reverse cumsum per stratum
reason: Confirmed O(nK) rescans in .breslow_hazard (helper_survival_fits.R:592-598) and .cox_neg_loglik_breslow_r (inference_survival_coxph.R:109-133, used by kk_cox_fully_fixed_null_fit). Already scheduled as algorithm_choice_audit.md TODO-18 (catalog §12 TODO-7) in v1.2.0-TODO-22; routing the null fit to compute_cox_neg_ll_only should be added to that item.

finding: Build the KK strat-Cox correlation-threshold design ladder lazily
reason: Confirmed eager: up to 12 drop_highly_correlated_cols + hardened QR rungs are built before any fit (inference_survival_KK_strat_cox.R:155-177). Lazy construction is bit-identical; cost unmeasured, so profile first. No existing TODO.

finding: Native weighted Efron Cox Newton for Bayesian bootstrap (coxdev-based)
reason: Bench, Phase 0 (run 44048167550, same EDI build, 20 ABBA blocks): not faster, ratio 3.13 (the coxdev-based weighted Efron fit is 3.1x slower than today's path; 95% interval -221% to -208%). Automatic reject (owner 2026-11-19). The native weighted Efron kernel in v1.1.0-TODO-63 is a separate item and stays.

finding: Weighted C++ Newton (probit/cloglog/logit) instead of MASS::polr for bootstrap surrogate fits
reason: globals.R:177-245 calls MASS::polr (model frame, glm start, BFGS reltol 1e-10) on every weighted draw for probit, cauchit, cloglog and the logistic surrogate (stereotype, adjacent-category, PPO); FixedOrdinalRegression already takes weights (ordinal_fixed_link_helpers.h:230) and fast_ordinal_regression_weighted_cpp exists (fast_ordinal_regression.cpp:387), but the probit/cloglog exports have no weights argument (fast_ordinal_probit_regression.cpp:300). Not covered by v1.2.0 TODO-17 (that replaces surrogates for GEE/stereotype/adjacent-category with native estimators) or audit TODO-27 (ZI/hurdle kernels).

finding: Newton (existing newton_raphson path) as default for concave cumulative-link fits
reason: Bench, Phase 0 (run 44048167550, same EDI build, 20 ABBA blocks): not faster, ratio 1.90 (Newton 90% slower than the default; results also moved by 0.0035 relative). Automatic reject (owner 2026-11-19). algorithm_choice_audit.md TODO-12 in v1.2.0-TODO-23 stays open for its own reasons.

finding: Tail-accurate cell-probability differences per link (rms celldiff) instead of F(u)-F(l) floored at 1e-12
reason: Robustness only, no speed gain; the cancellation and the 1e-12 floor (ordinal_fixed_link_helpers.h:258,285,343) are already recorded as a catalog section 2 incidental that 'only matters from extreme starts', and no fit failure has been traced to it. Revisit if a near-separated ordinal replicate failure is traced to the floor (it would then be a v1.0.6 false-convergence item).

finding: fastglm::fastglm_ordinal(nonparallel=) instead of VGAM::vglm for partial proportional odds
reason: Low confidence: no timings, fractional-weight behaviour undocumented (weights are frequency counts), estimator equivalence unknown, and fastglm_ordinal is a brand-new release (CRAN 0.1.4, 2026-11-11). It would add a dependency, so it would belong in v1.2.0+ with an owner decision; vglm is called at inference_ordinal_partial_proportional_odds.R:574,607. Revisit once the package has matured.

finding: Gate cloglog full-data 4-start multistart on a convergence certificate
reason: The cumulative cloglog likelihood is concave, so .cloglog_full_data_multistart (inference_ordinal_cloglog.R:1-44) only repairs solver non-convergence, yet it runs 4 extra fits on every fit_fun call (:304, :314), including replicates. It was added for a confirmed contamination bug (bug_fix_plans/v1_0_5/ordinal_cumulative_link_null_refit_multistart.md, ~line 477), so gating must reproduce that fix; catalog line 1817 already flags the 2-start null refit as 'papers over a solver failure'.

finding: Eigen selfadjointView rankUpdate (SYRK) for the per-replicate Gram in OLS rand bootstrap
reason: The same swap was benchmarked and dropped: performance_profiling_and_upgrades.md TODO-29 (fast_ols.cpp) found Eigen rankUpdate 4-6% slower than the full product at p=6, and TODO-118 found DSYRK wins only at p>=15. EDI's OLS kernels run at small p, and the Gram at rand_bootstrap_ols_parallel.cpp:76 is the same shape, so the prior measurement still holds.

finding: Cancellation-free centred form of the LMM per-group quadratic form W_g
reason: Robustness only, low confidence, and it matters only at v_b/v_e of about 1e6 or more; W_g = Q_g - (v_b/a_g) S_g^2 is at fast_gaussian_lmm.cpp:109-118 / :158. The natural time to change it is the profiled-LMM rewrite (audit TODO-32, v1.2.0-TODO-23), which reworks neg_ll_and_grad anyway.

finding: One cor() per call for the 12-rung correlation-threshold ladder, and cache the candidates
reason: drop_highly_correlated_cols (helper_model_matrix.R:113-136) recomputes cor() once or twice per rung, and the ladders call it 12 times per call (inference_survival_KK_lwa_cox_ivwc_abstract.R:180-183, inference_survival_KK_strat_cox.R:160, inference_survival_KK_rank_regr_ivwc_abstract.R:148, inference_mixin_kk_gee_shared.R:338-340). Catalog lines 1938 and 2098 note the Cox and GEE candidate lists are rebuilt on every call including every BB replicate though they do not depend on the weights; no release TODO schedules either fix.

finding: Single forced-front pivoted QR or column-append QR updates in qr_reduce_preserve_cols_cpp
reason: Already listed in audit TODO-29 ('qr_reduce_preserve_cols single factorization', v1.2.0-TODO-22, low-priority linear algebra). The keep-set is cached, so the path is cold, and a different pivot could change the keep-set on near-collinear designs; no new reason to raise its priority. (Was cited under v1.2.0-TODO-22.)

finding: p-value-only Fisher exact path (zhang_exact_fisher_pval_cpp or conf.int=FALSE)
reason: pval_exact_fisher (inference_indicidence_exact_fisher.R:109) is only reached from the user-level p-value at a given delta (:78); the CI comes from one fisher.test call, not from inversion, so there is no repeated-call hot path. Low value; the conf.int = FALSE change is trivial when the file is next touched.

finding: O(log n) boundary search for the minlike exact binomial p-value
reason: At EDI's discordant-pair counts the O(n) dbinom loop in zhang_exact_speedups.cpp::binom_two_sided_pval costs microseconds even inside the Zhang CI bisection (as the finding itself notes), so the win does not apply at EDI's sizes. Owner 2026-11-19: overruled the draft reject; scheduled as v1.2.0-TODO-245.

finding: Tail-only JT polynomial DP with reachable-range pruning
reason: Same item as audit TODO-15 (JT exact null by polynomial DP, catalog section 6 TODO-1), scheduled in v1.1.0-TODO-50 after the v1.0.5 TODO-90 size guard. The tail-pruning variant and the udist.go oracle are implementation notes for that item, not a new TODO.

finding: Exact finite sums for integer/half-integer df upper chi-square tail
reason: Catalog verdict for fast_gamma_functions.h fast_pchisq_upper is Keep (catalog line 1024), and the finding expects negligible end-to-end gain since each p-value follows a refit; the accuracy benefit is unquantified. Could ride with the accuracy batch (audit TODO-22, v1.1.0-TODO-50) if that is reopened.

finding: Eigenvalues-only GH nodes plus recurrence log-weights, in the shared cached GH rule
reason: Dedup and caching of the 4-6 GH copies is already scheduled (v1.4.0-TODO-11i part D; also audit TODO-29 in v1.2.0-TODO-22). The accuracy point is new and now relevant because the Poisson GLMM default rose to n_gh = 60 (audit re-review 2026-11-16, row C): add a log-weight check against a high-precision reference at n = 60/100 to that item rather than a separate TODO.

finding: Sufficient-statistic (pair/singleton stratum) evaluation of the Gaussian LMM likelihood
reason: Belongs with the profiled 1-D Gaussian LMM item (audit TODO-32, catalog section 4 TODO-3), scheduled in v1.2.0-TODO-23 on the A/B harness; the stratum blocks make every NLL/gradient and every fit_null delta O(p^2), independent of n. Add it as the evaluation layer of that prototype with the n in {50, 500, 5000} timing grid.

finding: Cache the multgee uniform local-odds-ratio structure across ladder rungs and draws
reason: Low confidence: the LOR estimation's share of an ordLORgee call is unmeasured, and the cache couples EDI to multgee's LORterm layout. The native ordinal GEE kernel that replaces multgee::ordLORgee is already scheduled (v1.2.0-TODO-2), which supersedes an interim cache. (Was cited under v1.2.0-TODO-2.)

finding: Regularized (sqrt(||g||)) Newton with LLT/LDLT and indefiniteness shift in optimize_likelihood_newton
reason: This is the modified-Newton safeguard for the shared optimize_likelihood_newton (catalog section 1 TODO-9, audit TODO-32), scheduled in v1.2.0-TODO-23; the trust-region engine (v1.2.0 TODO-203) is the alternative. The finding supplies a concrete parameter-free damping rule; also resolve the ignored warm_start_hessian there. Iterate paths change on nonconcave NB/beta/stereotype fits, so it needs the harness.

finding: Cluster-total collapse of the 60-node Poisson GLMM objective, gradient and Louis Hessian
reason: fast_poisson_glmm.cpp:198-205 computes exp(eta+b_k) over all n rows at every node and :276-283 does one weighted_crossprod per node, O(n*K*p^2); for the log link these collapse to per-group totals. The default rose from 20 to 60 nodes (2.3-2.8x cost, audit re-review 2026-11-16 row C), so this kernel's cost tripled. No release TODO covers it (adaptive GH, TODO-153, changes the rule instead).

finding: Adaptive or pseudo-adaptive GH for the 20-node logistic/clogit/engine and 7-node hurdle GLMMs
reason: Already the adaptive-quadrature item performance_profiling_and_upgrades.md TODO-153, carried in v1.2.0-TODO-11 (with a glmer(nAGQ=25) gate from v1.0.5-TODO-31). It changes the estimator (a different quadrature rule), so default changes need the owner's decision; add arXiv 2202.07864 (inconsistency of non-adaptive GH) and the Rizopoulos frozen-mode route to that item.

finding: Vectorize the fused score + X'WX loop (SIMD reduction hint or Eigen dot)
reason: score_weighted_crossprod_colwise_assign (_helper_functions_core.h:601-626) is a scalar pairwise reduction with no reduction hint on the logistic/probit IRLS hot path. The SIMD lane (v1.2.0-TODO-12, more_simd_optimization.md, which already discusses per-loop omp simd reductions) owns this kind of fix; add this loop as a named target with the n in {100, 500, 2000}, p in {2, 5, 10, 20} microbenchmark.

finding: Batched bounded-integer RNG (Lemire) for Fisher-Yates in random_balanced_init
reason: The shuffle is a negligible share of each greedy/D/A search draw (the O(n_T n_C) swap rounds dominate), so the end-to-end gain is about 1x, while it would change every seed-pinned design stream and its fixtures.

finding: One grouped rowsum pass instead of which(m_vec == pid) per pair, per replicate
reason: kk_pair_and_reservoir_bootstrap_weights (globals.R:262-290) runs vapply over pair ids with which(m_vec == pid), O(n^2/2) plus n/2 R closures, on every bootstrap replicate of the KK OLS, robust, quantile, cond-logit and passthrough classes (callers at inference_continuous_KK_ols_one_lik.R:488, inference_continuous_KK_robust_regr_one_lik.R:444, inference_all_KK_quantile_regr_one_lik_abstract.R:278, inference_mixin_kk_passthrough.R:222,233, inference_incidence_KK_cond_logit.R:67); build_combined_cpoisson_data has the same pattern (inference_count_KK_cond_poisson.R ~1903).

finding: O(n) closed-form Hodges-Lehmann variance from centred group sums
reason: Exact and more stable, but the only caller is compute_wilcox_matching_ivwc_bootstrap_parallel_cpp (fast_wilcox_hl.cpp:574-576), used by the legacy InferenceAllKKWilcoxIVWC (inference_all_KK_wilcox_ivwc.R:467). Low value; do it when that file is next touched for the HL SE scale fix.

finding: Profile-likelihood covariance for icenReg::ic_sp instead of 200 internal bootstrap refits
reason: inference_survival_coxph.R:472,734-736 calls ic_sp(model='ph', bs_samples=200), so each SE costs ~201 fits and consumes global RNG draws; the catalog options table (line 1896-1897) lists profile-likelihood SE but notes it 'requires a profile maximiser', which icsp2's vcov logic supplies. It changes the SE estimator (bootstrap to profile information), so it needs the owner's decision, and it would port LGPL code (GPL-compatible) or add a non-CRAN dependency.

finding: icenReg::ic_np (C++ EMICM, weights=) instead of interval::icfit EM for Turnbull stats
reason: Already audit TODO-28 (EMICM for the Turnbull NPMLE: initEMICM first, then icenReg::ic_np, whose weights= unblocks the interval-censored BB), scheduled in v1.1.0-TODO-50; icenReg is already a dependency. The JSS timings are supporting evidence; median/RMST A/B against icfit remains the gate.

finding: Pooled interval-censored NPMLE solved once per randomization test (icFIT= or wlr_trafo scores)
reason: Already audit TODO-11 (pooled-NPMLE scores once; gate: reproduce ictest on fixtures), scheduled in v1.2.0-TODO-22; call sites compute_shared_icen in inference_survival_log_rank.R and inference_survival_gehan_wilcox.R. The interim icFIT= + method='pclt' change is a cheaper first step inside that item.

finding: Exact closed-form delete-one-unit/cluster jackknife for least-squares estimators
reason: approximate_jackknife_distribution_beta_hat_T_private and approximate_bayesian_jackknife_distribution_beta_hat_T run n_units (or G) R6 refits even for mean-difference/OLS/Lin/WLS, which have the exact downdate beta^(g) = (X'X - X_g'X_g)^-1 (X'y - X_g'y_g); catalog rows 24/29 (lines 1581, 1586) record the refit loop as Keep and the jackknife-influence table has no exact-LS option. Same estimator, so no owner decision needed. Owner 2026-11-19: kept despite the Phase 0 bench verdict `not faster` (run 44048167550); its bench spec does not measure what this TODO is for (removing the n_units or G refits). Not an automatic reject.

finding: Linearized (CV3L) jackknife from per-unit scores/information as an opt-in
reason: Estimator change (first-order approximation; BCa a-hat and jackknife SE move), low confidence, and it needs per-unit score and information contributions that most EDI specs do not expose (the same obstacle the catalog records for the infinitesimal jackknife, line ~1676). The 'v1.0.6-TODO-7' the finding cites is unrelated (ModifiedPoisson ~1 at large n). Revisit after the exact LS jackknife lands and if per-unit hooks are added.

finding: Weighted Greenwood RMST SE by sort + reverse cumsum instead of O(n*D) vapply
reason: weighted_restricted_mean_se_diff builds n_j and d_j with vapply over unique times (inference_survival_rmst.R:386-387), O(n*D) per arm per BB replicate.
